description: Current-state lease abstract from a lease and its amendments, with amendment precedence, as of as_of. Give each document's pages with the candidates you extracted (checked exactly as doc_verify_facts checks them), or the facts doc_verify_facts already returned for it (without pages only the value against its quote is rechecked, marked quote_on_page: false). Documents may come in any order: give the lease role original and each amendment role amendment with its effective_date (without a role the lease is inferred only when that is unambiguous, otherwise it is an input error; two or more amendments need effective dates). The original applies first, then amendments by effective_date; a later document's value for a predicate controls, and the earlier one moves to history and is linked through supersedes. An amendment effective after as_of is pending: its values are listed under pending and pending_facts with a warning and do not control. A rent schedule restated from a later date keeps the earlier steps before it (carried_forward). Each field gives its value, the controlling document, page, quote and fact, the superseded history, conflicts (two different values from one document, or from two documents of the same rank), pending values and open_items (a candidate for that predicate in the controlling or a later document that needs review or was rejected, so the value may not be final). FactLot only orders what you extracted: it does not find terms you missed, and an amendment that changes a term without restating it ("extended by 24 months") needs the resulting value extracted with that sentence as its quote, which the quote check will hold for review if the date is not written there.

as_of.description: Date the facts are stated as of (YYYY-MM-DD), usually today.

documents.description: The lease and its amendments. Each needs pages with candidates or facts, or facts alone.

candidates.description: Values you extracted, each with its quote and page.

commencement.description: Only for lease.base_rent_schedule written by lease year (steps {lease_years: [1, 5], annual_rent_psf}): the commencement date the step dates are derived from, with its own quote. FactLot checks it like a lease.commencement_date candidate and derives each step: Lease Year N runs from the (N−1)th anniversary of the commencement date to the day before the next. If it does not verify, the schedule stays in needs_review.

page.description: 1-based page of this document the quote is on (it may differ from the rent table's page).

quote.description: Verbatim text that states the commencement date, at least 12 characters.

confidence.description: Your confidence 0–1. Below 0.8 the candidate goes to needs_review even if it verifies.

confirmation.description: A person's confirmation of the parts of the value no quote can prove (a true/false value, an enum such as a CAM cap method or kick-out party, a paraphrased summary). With it, a candidate whose only gaps are such parts is verified with method human_verified: the parts the quote confirmed are listed under checked and the rest under confirmed_by_person. It never overrides a quote that is not on the page, a number or date the quote does not state, or a confidence below 0.8.

at.description: When the person confirmed it: YYYY-MM-DD, or an ISO 8601 timestamp with offset. A date is recorded on the fact as that day at 00:00 UTC.

by.description: The name or role of the PERSON who read the clause and confirmed the value, e.g. "J. Smith, lease administrator". FactLot does not authenticate it. Never set this for a value no person has read: an agent must not confirm its own extraction.

note.description: What the person checked; returned with the result (the fact schema has no field for it).

predicate.description: Dotted lower_snake predicate. Use an Ingest predicate (lease.expiration_date, lease.base_rent_schedule, ...) for its value-shape and quote rules; any other predicate gets the generic rules.

quote.description: Verbatim text from the page that states the value, at least 12 characters. Copy it exactly; only whitespace, line breaks, letter case and typographic quotes and dashes may differ.

section.description: Section or clause as written, e.g. "§4.2(b)".

value.description: The value you read, in the predicate's shape: dates YYYY-MM-DD, money and areas as plain numbers (1250000, not "$1.25M"), shares and rates as decimals (0.03 for 3%).

effective_date.description: Amendment effective date (YYYY-MM-DD), required when there are two or more amendments: they apply in date order, and amendments effective the same day do not supersede each other (a different value is a conflict). An amendment effective after as_of is pending: its values are listed under pending and do not control the current abstract. Becomes valid_from on its facts.

facts.description: Facts doc_verify_facts already returned for this document. With pages, each is checked again; without pages (to stay under the request size limit), only its value against its quote is checked and the abstract marks it quote_on_page: false.

items.description: A FactLot fact, as doc_verify_facts returned it.

ocr_pages.description: Optional: pages (1-based) whose text came from OCR rather than the file's text layer (doc_read_pdf and factlot.read_pdf report them). Facts and citations on these pages carry ocr: true, so a reviewer checks the scan.

pages.description: The document's text, one string per page in order: pages[0] is page 1. Send the text as extracted (from the PDF text layer or OCR), not a summary; quotes are matched against it.

items.description: The text of one page, exactly as extracted.

role.description: Give it. Without one, a document is the original only when no document is marked original and it is the only one without a role (or without a role and an effective_date); otherwise it is an amendment, and input that leaves the original unclear is an error. Input order is never used.

sha256.description: Optional SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the original file. When given, document_id is fl:document:sha256-<this>, the same ID id_document gives the file; FactLot cannot check that the pages came from that file. Without it, document_id is the SHA-256 of the pages joined by form feeds (\f).

title.description: Document title for citations, e.g. "First Amendment to Lease".

subject.description: FactLot URN the facts are about, e.g. your lease's fl:lease:… ID. Default: the document ID.

name: doc_abstract_lease
title: Lease abstract with amendments
